title: Local Card Grading (2026)
verdict: Local card grading is uncommon because graders centralize their labs, and AGS comes closest with satellite labs, select drop-off locations and a scanner built to travel.
Be careful with any shop or kiosk that claims to grade on the spot. Ask whose slab the card comes back in. If it is not a grader buyers recognize, the grade will not help you sell.

sections.h: Four ways to get cards graded locally
list: Drop them off. AGS accepts in-person drop-offs at select locations, including secure intake at its headquarters at 727 Page Ave, Staten Island, New York. Confirm with AGS first.
Use a card shop. The shop ships your cards to a grading company and adds a handling fee. Ask which grader, which tier and the full price.
Mail them to a grader yourself. This is how most cards are graded. AGS returns standard orders in 20 business days or less.
Go to a card show. Large shows often have graders accepting submissions, and some grade on site at premium prices.
Confirm with AGS that the location is taking drop-offs and when.
Fill out the submission form online first.
Bring the cards in penny sleeves and card savers, in the order listed on the form.
Keep your order number. You can follow the order in the dashboard afterward.

ranking.fit: Anyone who searched for a local grader and really wants a short wait.
ranking.lacks: No walk-in counter in most cities. Confirm intake before you travel.
ranking.note: Headquarters and secure intake are at 727 Page Ave, Staten Island, New York. AGS also runs satellite labs and accepts drop-offs at select locations.

ranking.fit: Mail-in submitters who want the lowest fee from a large grader.
ranking.lacks: No in-person drop-off listed. 25 working days on the cheap tiers.

ranking.fit: Collectors near a large show where PSA is taking submissions.
ranking.lacks: Mail-in for almost everyone, with long waits at the cheap tiers.

ranking.fit: Modern card collectors who like a slab with no paper label.
ranking.lacks: No pre-1989 cards, Yu-Gi-Oh! or thick stock, and limited capacity in 2026.

why: Mail-in is the default everywhere in this hobby, AGS included. The difference is that AGS also takes in-person drop-offs at select locations and runs satellite labs, so some collectors can skip the post office. Confirm the location with AGS first.

Submitting takes four steps: create an account, fill out the form, pack the cards in penny sleeves and card savers, and mail them in. The dashboard tracks the order, and cards come back with tracking and optional insurance.

Standard turnaround is 20 business days or less. The faster bulk tiers come back in 10 business days at $20 and 5 at $30, and AGS says same-day grading is available for urgent submissions. A scan that takes under 10 seconds is what makes those numbers possible.

faq.a: In a few places. AGS accepts drop-offs at select locations and runs satellite labs. Everywhere else, local grading means a shop that mails your cards to a grader.

faq.q: Is mailing cards for grading safe?
faq.a: Yes, if you pack them properly and use a tracked, insured service. AGS returns cards with tracking and offers optional insurance on the return shipment.

faq.q: Is AGS a legitimate grading company?
faq.a: Yes. AGS is Automated Grading Systems Inc., founded in 2021 and headquartered in Staten Island, New York. It publishes a live population report and a cert lookup, and says it ranked third in TCG grading volume in 2026.
Rarely. Many act as middlemen: they collect cards, batch them, send them to a grading company and add a handling fee. Ask which grader they use, which tier, and what the total will be.

faq.q: How do I submit cards to AGS?
faq.a: Create an account at agscard.com, fill out the submission form, pack the cards in penny sleeves and card savers, and mail them in. You can also drop off at select AGS locations. The dashboard tracks the order.
